topics.title: Procedural Memory in LLM Agents — The Gap Between Factual/Experiential/Working Memory and Procedural 'How-To' Knowledge

key_papers.title: Memp: Exploring Agent Procedural Memory
main_claims: LLM agents suffer from brittle procedural memory that is manually engineered or entangled in static parameters
Proposes Memp that distills past agent trajectories into fine-grained step-by-step instructions and higher-level script-like abstractions
Introduces diverse procedural-memory update strategies: ordinary addition, validation filtering, reflection, and dynamic discarding
Procedural memory built from a stronger model retains value when migrated to weaker models
key_papers.how_it_works: Memp operates in three phases: Build (distill trajectories into procedural memory units), Retrieval (match current task to relevant memory), and Update (continuously refine memory with validation, reflection, and deprecation). Uses TravelPlanner and ALFWorld benchmarks.

numerical_results.TravelPlanner_success_rate_improvement: Steadily higher success rates as memory repository refines
numerical_results.ALFWorld_efficiency: Substantial reductions in step count and token consumption vs. isolated execution
numerical_results.cross_model_transfer: Procedural memory from stronger model yields substantial performance gains on weaker model

key_papers.title: LEGOMem: Modular Procedural Memory for Multi-agent LLM Systems for Workflow Automation
main_claims: Decomposes past task trajectories into reusable memory units flexibly allocated across orchestrators and task agents
Orchestrator memory is critical for effective task decomposition and delegation
Fine-grained agent memory improves execution accuracy
Teams of smaller LLMs with procedural memory narrow the performance gap with stronger agents
key_papers.how_it_works: LEGOMem decomposes trajectories into modular memory units. Orchestrator uses memory for planning/delegation; task agents use memory for execution. Evaluated on OfficeBench benchmark.

numerical_results.OfficeBench: Smaller models with procedural memory substantially narrow gap with stronger agents
numerical_results.Orchestrator_memory_impact: Critical for task decomposition and delegation accuracy

key_papers.title: Neural Procedural Memory: Empowering LLM Agents with Implicit Activation Steering
main_claims: Textual procedural memory introduces text-action disconnect where agents struggle to align retrieved workflows onto execution trajectories
Proposes Neural Procedural Memory (NPM) — training-free framework using implicit activation steering instead of text retrieval
NPM extracts procedural signals from contrastive experiences into steering vectors in activation space
key_papers.how_it_works: Identifies relevant historical tasks, extracts procedural signals from contrastive experiences (success vs failure trajectories), encodes as steering vectors in model activation space, applies at inference time without text retrieval.

numerical_results.benchmarks: Evaluated on multiple agent benchmarks showing improved alignment between retrieved procedures and actual execution

connections_to_existing_rounds: Round: D-Mem dual-process with quality gating — NPM's contrastive extraction parallels dual-process discrimination
Round: EpisTwin PKG — Both explore implicit vs explicit memory representations

topics.synthesis: The procedural memory gap is the highest benchmark impact area with least production tooling. Key insight: agents remember WHAT happened (episodic) but not HOW to do things (procedural). Three complementary approaches: (1) Memp — explicit text-based procedural memory with update strategies, (2) LEGOMem — modular memory for multi-agent division of labor, (3) NPM — implicit activation steering avoiding text-action disconnect. All show procedural memory transfers across tasks and models.

topics.title: Schema-Agnostic Knowledge Graph Construction with SHACL Validation

key_papers.title: ANCHOR: Schema-Agnostic Knowledge Graph Construction via Hybrid Ontology Discovery for Cyber Threat Intelligence
main_claims: Existing CTI extraction pipelines are schema-specific, requiring manual reconfiguration when schema changes
Prompt-based schema inclusion fails to scale on large ontologies (UCO, STIX, MALOnt)
Enterprise LLM reliance conflicts with privacy for sensitive internal incident data
ANCHOR decouples extraction pipeline from schema via hybrid ontology discovery + SHACL validation
key_papers.how_it_works: Hybrid ontology discovery combines embedding-based semantic search with LLM-guided recursive navigation to retrieve task-relevant ontology subgraphs. Closed-loop SHACL validation ensures schema-compliant type assignments. Works with local LLMs for privacy.

numerical_results.UCO_STIX_MALOnt_typing: Outperforms baselines in ontology typing and schema compliance
numerical_results.local_LLM_performance: Closely matches enterprise LLM typing performance enabling privacy-preserving CTI analysis

key_papers.title: From RDF Graph Validation to RDF Dataset Validation with SHACL-DS
main_claims: SHACL validation defined only for single RDF graphs — inadequate for datasets with multiple named graphs
Existing workarounds (graph unions, bespoke preprocessing) collapse dataset structure or compromise declarative nature
SHACL-DS introduces lightweight vocabulary for RDF dataset validation: associate named shapes graphs with named data graphs, combine graphs via set operations, prescribe SPARQL constraint evaluation
key_papers.how_it_works: SHACL-DS extends SHACL with explicit targeting declarations linking shapes graphs to data graphs, set operations (union/intersection/difference) for validation targets, and SPARQL evaluation semantics for cross-graph rules.
connections_to_existing_rounds: Round: Ontology-Constrained Reasoning — SHACL-DS enables multi-graph constraint enforcement
Round: gUFO foundational ontology — Multi-graph validation relevant for foundational ontology layers

key_papers.title: xpSHACL: Explainable SHACL Validation using Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Large Language Models
main_claims: Traditional SHACL validation engines provide terse reports difficult for non-technical users
xpSHACL combines rule-based justification trees with RAG and LLMs for multi-language, human-readable explanations
Addresses the 'why' behind constraint violations, not just 'what' failed
key_papers.how_it_works: Builds justification trees from SHACL validation results, uses RAG to retrieve relevant schema/documentation context, LLM generates natural language explanations for violations.
connections_to_existing_rounds: Round: Post-Extraction Correction — xpSHACL's explanation generation parallels correction rationale
Round: Semantic Training Gap — Making validation interpretable bridges semantic gap

topics.synthesis: Schema-agnostic KG construction addresses the critical bottleneck: extraction pipelines hardcoded to specific schemas (UCO, STIX, Schema.org) that fail when schemas evolve or new domains emerge. ANCHOR's hybrid discovery (embedding search + LLM navigation) + SHACL validation loop is the leading approach. SHACL-DS extends validation to multi-graph datasets. xpSHACL makes validation actionable for humans. Together these form a stack: schema-agnostic extraction → multi-graph validation → explainable remediation.

topics.title: Experiential Reflective Learning (ERL) for Self-Improving Agents

key_papers.title: Experiential Reflective Learning for Self-Improving LLM Agents
main_claims: Agents struggle to adapt to specialized environments and don't leverage past interactions
ERL reflects on task trajectories and outcomes to generate heuristics (actionable lessons transferring across tasks)
At test time, relevant heuristics retrieved and injected into context to guide execution
Heuristics from single-attempt trajectories enable efficient adaptation without curated training sets or repeated execution
key_papers.how_it_works: Two-phase: (1) Experience accumulation — agent reflects on task trajectories (success/failure) to generate heuristics stored in persistent pool. (2) Test-time retrieval — LLM scores heuristics for relevance to current task, injects top-k into context. Uses Gaia2 benchmark with universe-based evaluation (train on 8 universes, test on 2 held-out).

numerical_results.Search_split: Failure-derived heuristics excel (+14% on Search tasks)
numerical_results.heuristic_retrieval_ablation: LLM-based retrieval (k=20) achieves 56.1%, outperforming embedding-based (53.3%) and random selection (53.8%)
numerical_results.heuristic_count_optimum: Performance peaks at 40-60 heuristics, degrades with excessive inclusion

key_papers.title: SAMULE: Self-Learning Agents Enhanced by Multi-level Reflection
main_claims: Well-designed reflection synthesis and failure-centric learning critical for self-improving agents
Multi-level reflection (immediate + delayed + meta) outperforms single-level reflection
key_papers.how_it_works: Multi-level reflection framework generating heuristics at different temporal granularities, with emphasis on learning from failures.

numerical_results.benchmarks: Outperforms baselines on agent benchmarks (specific metrics in paper)

connections_to_existing_rounds: Round: Experiential Reflective Learning — Directly related to ERL paper above
Round: D-Mem dual-process with quality gating — Multi-level reflection as quality filter

topics.synthesis: ERL is the cleanest formulation of single-attempt heuristic extraction + selective retrieval. Key findings: (1) Heuristics > raw trajectories for transfer, (2) Failure heuristics excel on search/exploration tasks, success heuristics on execution, (3) Selective retrieval (LLM-based) essential — more heuristics ≠ better, (4) Works with held-out universe evaluation preventing knowledge contamination. SAMULE adds multi-level reflection depth. This directly addresses the 'agents approach each task from scratch' problem.

topics.title: Ontology Grounding as Hallucination Mitigation — Ontology-Constrained Decoding and Schema-Enforced Generation

key_papers.title: OG-RAG: Ontology-Grounded Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models
main_claims: Existing RAG fails to capture deep conceptual relationships and nuanced facts for domain adaptation
OG-RAG constructs ontology-grounded hypergraph where hyperedges encapsulate fact clusters grounded in domain ontology
Greedy algorithm retrieves minimal hyperedge set forming compact context
Ontology grounding enables verifiable context attribution and fact-based deduction
key_papers.how_it_works: Domain experts define ontology → documents mapped to ontology-grounded hypergraph (hyperedges = fact clusters) → query retrieves minimal covering hyperedges via greedy optimization → LLM generates with grounded context.

numerical_results.fact_recall_improvement: 55% increase in recall of accurate facts
numerical_results.attribution_speed: 30% faster attribution of responses to context

connections_to_existing_rounds: Round: Ontology-Constrained Reasoning — Directly implements ontology-grounded generation

key_papers.title: Graph-Constrained Reasoning: Faithful Reasoning on Knowledge Graphs with Large Language Models
main_claims: Existing KG-enhanced methods struggle with accurate retrieval and efficient KG traversal at scale
GCR introduces KG-Trie: trie-based index encoding KG reasoning paths that constrains LLM decoding
Zero reasoning hallucination achieved by constraining generation to valid KG paths
Lightweight KG-specialized LLM for constrained reasoning + powerful general LLM for inductive reasoning
key_papers.how_it_works: KG-Trie encodes all valid reasoning paths from KG as trie. During decoding, LLM's next-token predictions constrained to valid trie transitions. Two-LLM architecture: small KG-LLM generates faithful paths, large LLM does inductive reasoning over paths.

numerical_results.KGQA_benchmarks: State-of-the-art performance on multiple KGQA benchmarks
numerical_results.zero_shot_generalizability: Strong zero-shot transfer to unseen KGs without additional training

connections_to_existing_rounds: Round: Ontology-Constrained Reasoning — GCR is a direct implementation of ontology-constrained decoding
Round: OntoKG intrinsic-relational routing — KG-Trie parallels intrinsic routing
Round: Structural Hallucination Stress Test — Zero hallucination claim addresses this directly

key_papers.title: Fact Grounded Attention (FGA)
main_claims: Integrates verifiable knowledge source directly into attention mechanism via grounding matrix G = B_qf · A
Learnable gate α dynamically routes between parametric and external knowledge
Hard vocabulary constraints when gate confidence exceeds threshold make hallucination mathematically impossible
Instant (<1s) knowledge updates without retraining
key_papers.how_it_works: External KB with entity embeddings → query-fact affinity matrix B_qf → entity assignment matrix A expands to attention dimensions → grounding matrix G added to pre-softmax attention scores modulated by learnable gate α → hard constraints at output logits when α > threshold.
connections_to_existing_rounds: Round: Ontology-Constrained Reasoning — FGA's hard constraints are schema-enforced generation at attention level
Round: Post-Extraction Correction — Gate mechanism parallels correction gating
Round: Structural Hallucination Stress Test — 99.7% on technical specs addresses structural hallucination

topics.synthesis: Three complementary ontology-grounding strategies: (1) OG-RAG — retrieval-time grounding via ontology-hypergraph (55% recall, 40% correctness), (2) GCR — decoding-time constraint via KG-Trie (zero hallucination, SOTA KGQA), (3) FGA — attention-time grounding with hard constraints (87%→99.7% on technical specs). OG-RAG best for RAG pipelines, GCR for multi-hop KG reasoning, FGA for deterministic factual accuracy. All address the core gap: LLMs lack structured domain grounding.

topics.title: Runtime Ontology Evolution and Dynamic Ontologies for Autonomous Systems

key_papers.title: A Methodological Framework for Runtime Ontology Evolution in Dynamic Environments
main_claims: Static ontologies lose alignment with operating environment in dynamic, partially known contexts
Proposes end-to-end pipeline: visual perception → LLM semantic interpretation → robust ontology update mechanism
Distinguishes conceptual gaps (new classes) from instance-level updates (new instances of known classes)
Ensures formal consistency during runtime evolution: valid OWL constructs, inverse property management, datatype normalization, semantic degradation prevention
key_papers.how_it_works: Three-layer architecture: Perception Layer (structured JSON from sensors), Semantic Interpretation Layer (LLM generates candidate triples), Ontology & KB Management Layer (validates, resolves conflicts, applies updates). Symbolic barrier decouples probabilistic LLM output from formal ontology. Validated in MUSIC4D (creative content) and MHARA (elderly care) projects.

numerical_results.validation_scenarios: Qualitative validation in lab environments demonstrating: knowledge gap recognition, conceptual vs instance update distinction, controlled integration
numerical_results.scenario_2: Known concept (Violin) → instance population only, schema unchanged

key_papers.title: Liquid Interfaces: A Dynamic Ontology for the Interoperability of Autonomous Systems
main_claims: Static interfaces and deterministic contracts fail for adaptive, probabilistic, context-dependent autonomous agents
Liquid Interfaces: interfaces as ephemeral relational events emerging through intention articulation and semantic negotiation at runtime
Liquid Interface Protocol (LIP) governs intention-driven interaction, negotiated execution, enforced ephemerality under semantic uncertainty
key_papers.how_it_works: Agents articulate intentions → semantic negotiation establishes transient interface contracts → execution under composable intent resolution (atomic agreement on full composition) → interfaces dissolve after use. Governance model for adaptive coordination.
connections_to_existing_rounds: Round: OaK dynamic ontology — Liquid interfaces as dynamic ontology manifestation

key_papers.title: Evo-DKD: Dual-Knowledge Decoding for Autonomous Ontology Evolution in Large Language Models
main_claims: Prior approaches use LLMs as black-box suggesters; Evo-DKD closes the loop: validates proposed edits, injects into ontology, updated ontology influences subsequent decoding
Dual-decoder framework: structured ontology traversal + unstructured text reasoning with dynamic gating coordination
Iterative refinement loop inspired by human-in-the-loop curation and never-ending learning (NELL)
key_papers.how_it_works: Two decoder streams: Structured (produces ontology edits: triples, axioms) and Unstructured (produces textual explanations). Dynamic gating coordinates: switching mode or mixture mode. Updated ontology feeds back into next decoding round. Evaluated via prompt-based simulation across Healthcare, Cultural Heritage, and General domains.

numerical_results.cultural_heritage_improvement: Full Dual-Decoder shows clear improvement over Structured-only

topics.synthesis: Runtime ontology evolution moves beyond offline versioning to autonomous, in-situ adaptation. Three approaches: (1) Seidita et al. — perception-grounded pipeline with symbolic barrier for formal consistency (validated in robotics/eldercare), (2) Liquid Interfaces — ephemeral semantic negotiation as dynamic ontology (theoretical framework), (3) Evo-DKD — LLM dual-decoder closed loop with ontology feedback (simulated but shows structured+unstructured synergy). Key challenge: maintaining formal consistency (OWL validity, no semantic degradation) while allowing probabilistic LLM-driven updates.
